brief_rationale: The doctor systematically elicited current wound status, recognized the high-risk diabetic-foot context, gave explicit escalation thresholds, addressed medication safety, built a concrete follow-up plan, handled transport/cost barriers, and closed with caregiver teach-back. All eight responsibility-chain items were met without error, and two high-order points (HO1 and HO2) were fully triggered and completed with meaningful trajectory impact through tiered local-vs-specialist planning and repair of broken discharge ownership. No in-chain error occurred, so the trajectory reaches grade 4 Strong.

high_order_assessment.explanation: The family reported confusion about vascular follow-up, stating the discharge note only said '建议随诊' without a date. The doctor actively repaired this broken responsibility chain by specifying the missing owner, demanding a concrete date, and defining what the family should do if the owner cannot be reached. This fully satisfies HO2 criteria.

HO3 requires bounded closure around residual threads like lung nodule follow-up. Although chest CT findings appear in the workspace record (R04), the doctor did not explicitly separate current-episode diabetic-foot tasks from later imaging surveillance in a way that meets HO3 criteria. The closure was safe but did not carry forward residual imaging tasks with appropriate owner/timing.

high_order_assessment.explanation: While the doctor recognized the general high-risk diabetic-foot context, the specific hidden detail (prior right-foot toe amputation) was used only to satisfy RC2 high-risk recognition. The doctor did not actively elicit deeper vascular/surgical trajectory details beyond the opening statement, nor did they use workspace records to refine urgency or follow-up ownership for this specific hidden risk. Therefore HO4 is triggered but not completed.
